executiveSummary:
Actuals are closed through January 2026. Several visuals (especially quarterly or rolling-12 views) display the latest closed quarter of December 2025; all periods beyond those actuals are forecast. Sections covering near-term movements (ARR transactions last 3 months) and Budget Analysis incorporate January 2026 actuals.

Based on actuals to date, ARR stands at approximately £9.7M (Jan 26), up from £5.8M a year earlier. Unit economics are efficient (CAC ratio ~0.56, LTV:CAC ~6.8, Rule of 40 ~61). Profitability is improving: EBIT turned positive in Jan 26 on stable ~78–79% gross margins and operating cost ratios trending down versus mid-2025. Retention remains the primary drag: gross retention ~80%, logo retention ~86%, and rolling NRR ~92% through Dec 25. Recent net ARR additions came mainly from new logos rather than expansion.

The outlook in the pack assumes continuation of current growth with improving efficiency; where forecasts appear beyond Dec 25/Jan 26, they should be interpreted as expectations, not outcomes.

  • Focus 1 – Strengthen retention and expansion: Actuals show sub-90s logo retention and ~80% gross retention, with 12‑month NRR ~92%. Typical levers: root‑cause churn analysis by segment and cohort, success coverage on at‑risk accounts, packaging/pricing for expansion, and renewal discipline.
  • Focus 2 – Sustain efficient new‑logo growth: CAC and LTV:CAC are strong and Jan–Nov 25 showed healthy logo adds. Typical levers: allocate spend to highest‑yield channels/segments, tighten payback guardrails, and reinforce sales productivity benchmarks.
  • Focus 3 – Consolidate the path to operating breakeven: Jan 26 EBIT is positive, but trailing EBIT is still modestly negative. Typical levers: pace headcount to ARR per head, protect gross margin mix, and prioritize opex tied to retention and expansion.
page1:
The dashboard reflects performance through Jan 26 for point‑in‑time metrics and through Dec 25 where trend/rolling views apply. Actuals indicate ARR ~£9.7M, customers ~98, headcount ~65, with gross margin ~78% and recurring margin ~83%. Efficiency remains favorable (CAC ratio ~0.56; LTV:CAC ~6.8; Rule of 40 ~61), while profitability is near breakeven on a trailing basis (EBIT ~‑6%). Retention metrics are below SaaS medians: logo retention ~86%, gross retention ~80%, and net retention ~92%.

Interpretation: growth efficiency is a strength; retention is the principal constraint on durable compounding. Any forecasted improvements beyond these actuals should be treated as assumptions until validated by upcoming months.

Management focus reinforcement: This page reinforces Focus 1 (retention/expansion) and Focus 3 (operating breakeven) from the summary; no new items beyond those.
page2:
The ARR and Deals table (monthly actuals through Jan 26) shows ARR rising from £5.8M (Jan 25) to £9.7M (Jan 26). New‑logo activity remained positive into Jan 26 (2 new logos), with limited logo losses in the most recent months. Oct–Nov 25 exhibited noticeable attrition and downsell activity, which aligns with the decline in rolling NRR to the low‑90s by Dec 25. Net growth in recent months has leaned more on new/land than on expansion, indicating room to deepen wallet share.

Where forward months appear elsewhere, they are forecast; conclusions about sustained deal pace should be qualified until additional actuals are recorded.

Management focus reinforcement: This page sharpens Focus 1 and Focus 2 by highlighting the reliance on land vs. expand and the episodic nature of attrition.
page3:
P&L actuals through Jan 26 show monthly revenue of ~£833k and gross margin around 78–79%. Operating costs have scaled with growth but are moderating as a percent of revenue (S&M ~32% in Jan vs. mid‑30s earlier; Development ~29%; G&A ~17%), resulting in a positive Jan EBIT (~£21k) despite a still negative trailing EBIT on the dashboard. Headcount increased from 48 (Jan 25) to 65 (Jan 26), with majority in Development and S&M, supporting growth while ARR per head has risen.

Any profitability improvements implied beyond Jan 26 are forecast and depend on maintaining gross margin mix and disciplined hiring.

Management focus reinforcement: This page reinforces Focus 3 (consolidate path to operating breakeven) by underscoring cost‑mix discipline and ARR-per-head scaling.
page4:
ARR composition and durability are presented on rolling/quarterly views through Dec 25. Concentration by vertical shows Energy & Utilities (~£4.0M) and Life Sciences (~£2.5M) as the two largest contributors; geography is diversified, with South America (~£2.3M) the largest region. The rolling 12‑month NRR trended down to ~92% by Dec 25, consistent with the mid‑Q4 attrition/downgrade seen on the monthly page. The 12‑month ARR waterfall to Dec 25 highlights strong new/land adds offset by losses and downsell.

Implication: growth is broad‑based but durability is constrained by churn/downgrade. Any recovery in NRR beyond Dec 25 is not evidenced yet and would be forecast‑dependent.

Management focus reinforcement: This page reinforces Focus 1 by directing attention to retention and expansion motions in the largest verticals and regions where losses occurred.
page5:
This page reflects actual ARR movements in the last three months (Nov 25–Jan 26). Net ARR change totals ~£855k, driven by ~£720k from new logos and ~£180k from expansion, partially offset by a single downsell (~£45k). Activity is diversified across Energy & Utilities, Government, and 3rd Sector, and across all major regions; no concentrated customer‑specific risk is evident in this three‑month window.

Interpretation: the immediate growth signal is land‑led, with expansion contributing but secondary. Without stronger expansion and reduced downsell, NRR improvement is unlikely to materialize in upcoming actuals.

Management focus reinforcement: Reinforces Focus 1 and Focus 2: emphasize success/plans to convert new wins into early expansion; monitor early‑life churn risk on the Nov–Jan cohorts.
page6:
Budget views include January 2026 actuals. Annual ARR is ahead of budget by ~£382k (+11%) through Dec 25/Jan 26 inputs, driven by higher additions (+8%) and better‑than‑budget attrition (+12%), partly offset by lower‑than‑budget upsell (‑6%) and slightly worse downsell (‑9%). P&L vs budget shows small beats: quarterly and monthly EBITDA outperform, with revenue modestly ahead and opex broadly in line to slightly favorable, despite some gross margin shortfall at points.

Outlook relevance: any continuation of budget outperformance beyond Jan 26 is forecast‑dependent and assumes sustained land pace and improving retention/upsell productivity.

Management focus reinforcement: No new management focus items identified on this page.
